Prevention: Plant disease free seedlings from a certified nursery such as
Select well drained soils before planting.
Observe correct planting spaces of 1m by 1m to avoid overcrowding of plants.
Avoid watering the plants using overhead systems to reduce spread of disease
Do not compost any diseased plants for manure.
Use a slow release organic fertilizer to avoid excess nitrogen as young leafy plant parts are susceptible.
Monitoring: Look out for white powdery spots and deposits on the leaves,and flowers
Look out for curled leaves, buds and growing tips during late infection stage.
Look out for young shoots that wither and die back as severe infection causes defoliation.
Look out for wilting, distorted and dying leaves
Take action when 3 leaves per plant are infected.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Uproot infected plants and destroy by burning the infected debris.
